finding.claim: Negative amount on /transfer lets the caller take money from any existing account.
finding.source: JSON body field 'amount' via request.json at bank.py:10 (any client; no sign validation)
finding.sink: Balance mutations at bank.py:13 (caller credited) and bank.py:14 (recipient 'to' debited)

trace.note: amount read from request.json, may be negative
only guard is BAL[g.user] < amount; never true for negative amount, so abort skipped
BAL[to] += amount debits any existing victim account

finding.guards_checked: Only line 11 balance check; no amount > 0 check (contrast /withdraw line 21). Precondition: g.user set externally to the attacker's identity (not present in repo); victim account must exist in BAL.

verdict.guard_found: Only the balance check at bank.py:11 (BAL[g.user] < amount). It does not block negative amounts: a negative amount is never less than a non-negative balance, so abort(400) is skipped. No amount > 0 check exists in /transfer (contrast the check at bank.py:21 in /withdraw). No other control sits between the caller and the balance mutations at bank.py:13-14.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: amount is read from the JSON body at bank.py:10, the only guard at bank.py:11 is bypassed by a negative amount, bank.py:13 credits the caller, and bank.py:14 debits the existing account named by 'to'. The attacker only needs to be an authenticated user whose identity is placed in g.user, which the repo never sets, so that upstream auth is the one precondition I could not verify from this code.

finding.claim: NaN amount corrupts balances on /withdraw and /transfer and can bypass the balance check, enabling minting of credit.
finding.source: JSON body field 'amount' at bank.py:20 and bank.py:10; Python json accepts NaN literal by default
finding.sink: Balance writes at bank.py:23 (withdraw) and bank.py:13-14 (transfer)

trace.note: NaN <= 0 is False and BAL < NaN is False, so abort skipped
BAL[g.user] -= NaN makes caller balance NaN permanently
With NaN balance every < comparison is False, so transfer checks never abort; finite amounts can be sent to accomplice accounts

finding.guards_checked: Line 21 rejects amount <= 0 and insufficient balance only; no math.isfinite or numeric type check anywhere. Infinity is rejected by line 21, so only NaN passes. Preconditions: g.user set externally; an accomplice account exists.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only checks are bank.py:21 (`amount <= 0 or BAL[g.user] < amount`) and bank.py:11 (`BAL[g.user] < amount`). Both are plain comparisons that are False for NaN, so the abort is skipped. No isfinite or type check exists anywhere in the directory, which contains only bank.py.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: bank.py:20 reads amount, bank.py:21 lets NaN through because both NaN comparisons are False, bank.py:23 writes NaN to the caller's balance, and bank.py:11/13-14 let a NaN-balance account transfer finite amounts to an accomplice (`BAL[to] += amount`, bank.py:14). Flask's request.json uses Python's json, which accepts the NaN literal. The attacker only needs an ordinary account with g.user set (its setter is not in the repo, so this is an assumption) plus a second existing account they control, so this is not a privilege-gated flaw.

finding.claim: No authentication or identity source: g.user is never set, so authorization is undefined and the routes cannot serve successful requests as shipped.
finding.source: Any unauthenticated HTTP client reaching /transfer or /withdraw
finding.sink: All balance reads and writes keyed by g.user (bank.py:11, 13, 21, 23)

trace.note: BAL[g.user] evaluated; g.user never assigned in repo, so AttributeError is raised
same AttributeError on /withdraw for positive amounts, surfaces as HTTP 500

finding.guards_checked: No before_request hook, decorator, session or token check in the repo (grep for g.user, before_request, login_required, set_user). Could not verify deployed configuration; precondition finding, not a confirmed exploit.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only grep hits for g.user are bank.py:11, 13, 21 and 23, and there is no assignment, before_request hook, decorator, login_required, or set_user anywhere in the repo. Only bank.py exists. The routes at bank.py:7 and :18 have no decorators.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches: bank.py:11 reads BAL[g.user] and bank.py:21 reads it for positive amounts (short-circuit skips it when amount <= 0), while g.user is never assigned in the repo, so Flask raises AttributeError and the request returns 500. An anonymous client reaches both routes with no guard. The impact is limited to a 500 on these routes as shipped, and whether real auth exists depends on deployment code outside this repo, so this is a confirmed precondition gap rather than a demonstrated security exploit.

finding.claim: /transfer is not atomic: the sender is debited before the recipient lookup, so a nonexistent 'to' destroys the debited funds.
finding.source: JSON body field 'to' at bank.py:9 (attacker-chosen string)
finding.sink: Sender debit at bank.py:13 persisted before BAL[to] KeyError at bank.py:14

trace.note: BAL[to] raises KeyError for unknown account; no try/except or rollback, so debit persists and response is 500

finding.guards_checked: No existence check on 'to' before line 13; no exception handling; no transaction or rollback. Impact is self-destruction of funds plus broken conservation of money; attacker gains nothing directly.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only checks are the balance test at bank.py:11 (which covers the sender's funds, not the recipient) and the amount check at bank.py:12. There is no existence check on `to`, no try/except, and no rollback. Flask does not roll back the in-memory BAL dict when the handler raises.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches: `to` is read unvalidated at bank.py:9, the sender is debited at bank.py:13, and `BAL[to] += amount` at bank.py:14 raises KeyError for an unknown key after the debit has already been applied. The attacker only needs whatever access `/transfer` requires (g.user is set outside this file, so that gate is unverified here); the impact is limited to destroying the attacker's own funds, which the candidate already states.

finding.claim: Check-then-act race: concurrent requests can both pass the balance check and overdraw an account.
finding.source: Concurrent HTTP requests from one client, each with amount under the balance

trace.note: debit applied after check with no lock; another thread can pass line 11 in the window

finding.guards_checked: No lock, atomic update, or per-account serialization. Severity depends on server mode (threaded vs multi-worker), which is not visible in the repo; could not verify.

verdict.guard_found: none. No lock, atomic update, or per-account serialization exists in bank.py. The check at bank.py:11 and debit at bank.py:13 (and bank.py:21 and bank.py:23) are separate statements with no guard between them.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code (check at bank.py:11 and :21, unlocked debit at bank.py:13 and :23), and no guard exists, but whether the race is reachable depends on the server running multiple request threads in one process, which the repo does not show, and g.user is never set in this file, so the attacker's role cannot be determined either.
